What is an estimator in statistics, and how does it differ from an estimator statistic? Can you also explain different types of estimators and how they perform?
In the study of statistics, an estimator is a function of the observed data which is used to infer the value of an unknown parameter. An estimator statistic is a single value of an estimator. If there are multiple estimators available for a single parameter, then one can think of those as different estimator statistics. If point estimates are available for each of those estimators, then the single statistic corresponding to the point estimate with the smallest variation is the estimator statistic. Alternatively, one might choose an estimator statistic according to the requirement that its estimate will be as close to the true value as possible. Another estimator statistic is the value that occurs most frequently in the observations.

Different types of estimators that are most commonly used include the mode, the median, and the mean. The mean, while easy and versatile, is not robust, and may not provide meaningful results when there are values in the data that do not coherently fit with the surrounding data. A mean value can either be provided or used as a form of estimate, although such values should not be interpreted or used as results unless accompanied by an estimate of the estimator's uncertainty or error.

For example, if we have a dataset of salaries, the mean salary would be the sum of all salaries divided by the number of data points. The mode would be the most frequently occurring salary, and the median would be the middle value when the data is ordered. The mode and median can be more robust to outliers than the mean, but the mean can still be useful when all data points contribute equally to the result.

If \(X\) is infinite, there are more open sets in the discrete topology than there are elements in a basis for the discrete topology, which is impossible. This is due to the fact that the power set of an infinite set is uncountable, while the set of all finite subsets of a given infinite set is countable.
